source_text.body:
Write a 45-page medical imaging literature review
The author had Claude Code use arXiv/PubMed searches and supplied papers to write a ~13,800-word review with 113 citations, noting that good source papers mattered most.
·
Nov 11, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
In plan mode, Claude Code read one or two top-journal reviews to produce a style guide (CLAUDE.md). It then pulled the author's paywalled papers from Zotero through a Zotero MCP and searched arXiv and PubMed through MCPs. It drafted a review plan (IMPLEMENT.md), which the author checked by hand. Claude Code then wrote the draft without intervention.
How it went
The output was 45 pages, 13,813 words and 113 citations, all from arXiv, PubMed or the supplied papers, in Nature style. A plain one-line prompt gave a weak review. The author still has to review the draft and add figures.
Worth knowing
Paywalled papers must be downloaded by hand into Zotero. Don't point Claude Code at a local folder of PDFs, because a few papers can overflow the context.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Write a literature review of about [word count] words on [topic] using the papers in [folder] plus searches of arXiv and PubMed for gaps. Cite every claim with a numbered reference, and give me a reference list with links. When finished, list any claims you couldn't source well so I can check them.
Original source: https://agent.csdn.net/6a4e6726662f9a54cb8bf882.html
